title: Eyes of your heart (Ephesians 1:15–23)
hook: Paul prays their heart's eyes are enlightened
tomorrow: if grace is a free gift, why bother doing good at all?

segments.voice: That was the week of the table: a plate moved in Antioch, three pairs and a broken pattern, Abba, a yoke lifted, a slow harvest, and a blessing over everything. Yesterday's line: to the praise of his glory.
screen: `TO THE PRAISE OF HIS GLORY.` → `THE WEEK OF THE TABLE.`

segments.voice: When someone you love is struggling, the prayer list writes itself: the job, the test results, the rent. Paul has heard about these believers' faith and their love "unto all the saints," and he says he hasn't stopped: "Cease not to give thanks for you, making mention of you in my prayers." So what does he ask for? Not a fix. Not an easier week. He asks that they would see.
screen: `THE PRAYER LIST WRITES ITSELF.` → `MAKING MENTION OF YOU.` → `NOT A FIX: SIGHT.`

segments.voice: The King James reads: "The eyes of your understanding being enlightened." Other Greek copies have the word heart there, which is where today's title comes from. Either way, it's sight that works from the inside. Paul names three things he wants them to see. First, "what is the hope of his calling": where all this is going. Second, the riches of God's inheritance in the saints, which some readers hear as God counting his people as treasure. Third, "what is the exceeding greatness of his power to us-ward who believe." And he measures that power by Easter: the same strength that raised Christ from the dead and seated him above every name. Then the prayer lands on the church, a crowd of ordinary people, which he calls Christ's body, "the fulness of him that filleth all in all." Not a building. People, seen rightly. So his prayer for people he loves is mostly about their eyes. If they can see the hope, the worth and the power, they can face the week they actually have.
screen: `THE EYES OF YOUR UNDERSTANDING.` · `HOPE: WHERE IT'S GOING.` · `RICHES: GOD'S PEOPLE AS TREASURE.` · `POWER: THE SAME THAT RAISED CHRIST.` · then, large: `THE EYES OF YOUR HEART.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring one friend to mind, someone carrying something heavy right now. Instead of asking for the fix, wish them sight: hope they can't see yet, their own worth, strength for this week. If you pray, you can pray Paul's words over them: the eyes of your understanding being enlightened.
Eyes of your heart. Paul's picture of seeing from the inside: hope, worth and power that ordinary eyes miss.
Keep this line: the eyes of your heart, lit up for a friend. That's the week.
